Folks — quick triage notes from the runtime team: 
- Route observed: route-infer-2 (checkout model) saw queue length spike starting ~07:43 UTC.
- Evidence: KV cache misses increased (likely cold-shard surfacing) + concurrent requests scale hit the configured concurrency cap (100). The serving pool started applying backpressure which pushed up queueing time; once requests timed out we saw 502 downstream.
- No recent model rollout to route-infer-2 in the last 48h; however, autoscaler logs show a short delay in adding nodes during a small GC/eviction on one host.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (I’m executing now):
1) Increase concurrency cap on route-infer-2 from 100 -> 200 to allow more in-flight requests while we stabilize.
2) Shift 20% of incoming traffic for the Acme route to warm backup pool (route-infer-3) to drain the hot queue.
3) Enable short-lived prefix cache (30s) to reduce repeated KV fetches for identical warm prompts.

I’m attaching the console trace: https://redwood.console/reports/trace/ABC123 and a quick snapshot of the autoscaler events in the attached console_spike_link.txt.

Markus

Evelyn / Karthik —

Quick executive summary of the Acme incident (they are on a 10:00 call with a customer):
- Impact: ~8% error spike (502/503) and p99 latency increase to ~9–10s for checkout traffic between 07:43–07:55 UTC. Throughput reduction observed on customer side.
- Root cause (initial): Queueing/backpressure in route-infer-2 due to concurrency cap exhaustion + transient KV latency from vendor. Autoscaler added capacity but there was a short delay during a node eviction window.
- Mitigation executed: Markus increased concurrency caps, shifted 20% traffic to warm backup pool, and vendor reduced KV latency. Early telemetry shows p99 improving toward baseline.

Asks:
1) Approve a one-time temporary override of the concurrency guard (we will revert after stabilization) — this reduces customer impact but carries risk of higher GPU memory usage.
2) For customer communications: Jonas to provide a short write-up and offer one month of increased SLA credit if they want to formalize an incident credit.

I’ll keep this brief, will send a follow-up with metrics.

—Jonas

Quick follow-up and closure note now that we've validated stabilization: 
- What we changed: increased concurrency cap for route-infer-2 (100 -> 200) for a short window, shifted 20% of checkout traffic to route-infer-3, and the vendor applied a transient KV latency fix. We also enabled a short prefix cache for frequently requested prompts.
- Result: p99 fell back to ~420ms, error rate returned to baseline (~0.2% 5xx), and throughput normalized.
- Attachments: reroute-screenshot.png (shows traffic shift), console_spike_link.txt (snapshot of autoscaler events).

- We’ll run a targeted capacity test to validate steady-state behavior (week of May 4).

- Offer one month of enhanced SLA credit as a gesture; let me know if you prefer we start the paperwork.
